title: Bounds for Apparent Second-Law Violations in Quantum Trajectories
abstract: Negative stochastic entropy production is commonly called an apparent violation of the second law. In general quantum-trajectory dynamics, however, the physical entropy production $σ$ need not obey a forward detailed fluctuation theorem. A general arbitrary-coupling formulation identifies a dynamical-asymmetry term $σ^\ast$ that completes it into $Ω=σ+σ^\ast$, whose mean is $\langleΩ\rangle=Σ+Σ^\ast$. We prove that the likelihood-ratio sign is optimal among reversal-odd trajectory observables and use this fact to transfer an established sharp fluctuation-theorem floor to the tie-corrected physical sign statistic $Π_σ=\Pr(σ<0)+\Pr(σ=0)/2$. When $\Pr(σ=0)=0$, the result reads $\Pr(σ<0)\ge[1-\langleΩ\rangle/g(\langleΩ\rangle)]/2$, where $g$ is the inverse of $a\mapsto a\tanh(a/2)$. The physical integral fluctuation theorem simultaneously suppresses large negative events, producing a quantitative ``frequent but mild'' law, while the sign imbalance lower-bounds the hidden mean $Σ^\ast$. We formulate the measured-record protocol explicitly and illustrate and numerically audit the tie-corrected theorem in random finite-coupling collision models and a coherently driven qubit interacting with thermal ancillas.
summary: This paper develops rigorous bounds on apparent violations of the Second Law in quantum trajectories using advanced fluctuation theorems. By defining a completed entropy $\Omega$, it shows that the probability of observing negative entropy production ($\sigma < 0$) is quantitatively constrained by this completed observable's mean value. This provides a deep theoretical understanding of how measurement and environment coupling enforce thermodynamic constraints.
main_problem: The paper establishes rigorous bounds for apparent violations of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, specifically concerning negative stochastic entropy production in quantum trajectories.
main_result: It derives a quantitative lower bound ($\Pi_\sigma \ge L(\langle\Omegaangle)$) showing that apparent violations are constrained by the completed entropy and dynamical asymmetry, even when standard fluctuation theorems do not strictly apply to $\sigma$ alone.
method: The analysis employs path reversal techniques, general arbitrary-coupling formulations, and transfers established fluctuation theorem floors from a completed observable ($\Omega$) to the physical sign statistic ($\Pi_\sigma$).
model_or_system: The theory is applied to quantum trajectories describing open evolution, modeled using random finite-coupling collision ensembles or coherently driven qubits interacting with thermal ancillas.
key_observables: Physical entropy production ($\sigma$), dynamical-asymmetry term ($\sigma^*$), completed entropy ($\Omega$), and the tie-corrected physical sign statistic ($\Pi_\sigma$).
important_parameters: The bound depends on the mean of the completed observable, $\langle\Omegaangle$, which controls the severity of the constraint.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the path law satisfying a product identity and the general applicability of fluctuation theorems to the completed observable $\Omega$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the derived inequality ($\Pi_\sigma \ge \Pi_\Omega \ge L(\langle\Omegaangle)$) using results from both random collision models and coherently driven qubit systems.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of apparent violations, develops the mathematical framework relating $\sigma$ to $\Omega$, proves the optimality of the likelihood-ratio sign, derives the core inequality ($\Pi_\sigma \ge L(\langle\Omegaangle)$), and finally validates this result using two distinct physical models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool for quantifying non-equilibrium thermodynamics in open quantum systems by linking apparent violations to measurable dynamical asymmetries, which is crucial for understanding measurement backaction and irreversible processes.
